Yep, I've made one in win32 earlier this month for that exact reason. It's always amusing seeing DeepSeek's CoT realise it's running inside NT 4.0 once it does a directory listing. linzhangrun · Nov 21, 2026

Seriously speaking, I feel the market is sorely lacking an Agent for the large number of existing devices running WinXP, Win7, and the like. Not for developing on them, but for all kinds of debugging work it would be very useful; nowadays I'm used to just directing an Agent for everything.

linzhangrun · Nov 21, 2026

Almost all agents require Windows 10 1809 or later. Debugging issues on older devices often turns out to be a real headache, and the only option is to get SSH working.

anthk · Nov 21, 2026

There are Golang ports for WXP and up (check the Reticulum-go GH repo and the users), and there's MIn-C as a port of core OBSD tools for XP (Unix tools, compiler, vi, openssh and a bunch more).

egeozcan · Nov 21, 2026

Couldn't agents just Remote Desktop or ssh into them?

For seriously older stuff, I'd run the disk image in a VM.

If they interact with legacy systems and/or virtualizing is no option and/or they have no internet access, a simple USB-to-COM adapter can create wonders. I remeber doing that on a win3.1 machine using TERMINAL.EXE many many years ago.

linzhangrun · Nov 21, 2026

A typical scenario is that you walk into a small company and find they're still using Windows 7 or an early version of Windows 10. Then you have to help them deal with all sorts of problems.

ulrikrasmussen · Nov 21, 2026

In general, I've wondered whymost (all?) harnesses perform the API calls to the provider from the same machine that runs the tools. Why not have a client/server architecture? Then one session could talk to as many tool harnesses as it wanted to and you wouldn't have this kind of arbitrary limit of the session being tied to one specific workspace.
